Layout / Design: 1.	Alignment and spacing: All the elements on the piece, such as texts, images, or graphic elements, should be exactly consistent and aligned to the margins/guides or with each other. Spacing of the elements should be accurate and consistent too (unless it is intentional)
2.	The elements should be neatly placed, for example, the lines of the tables end as expected, and the images border doesn´t exceed the expected placement
items.detail:
If we start an asset design from scratch, we have to pay a lot of attention to the content alignment and general design layout.
If we discover an obvious error on the alignment and on the general layout on an inherited piece, we can request to correct it. But this requires prior agreement with the PM and/or CP. If the alignment or layout error is minimum, we should correct it without previous notification.

items.label:
Measurements: Make sure the width, height, margins, and safe area match the Brief
•	Remember to use Inches*
•	For big prints, standard scales could be used  
o	25%, 50%, 100%
o	1 inch = 2 inches (1" = 2")
o	1 inch = 4 inches (1" = 4")
o	1 inch = 1 foot (1" = 12")
*In the US, a period (.) is used to separate decimals in measurements
